pairs.difference: A Broom is a dry jhadu for sweeping dust; a Mop is wet, a pocha for wiping the floor.
A Pillow goes under your head on the bed; a Cushion sits decoratively on the sofa.
A Curtain is fabric that slides sideways; Blinds are slats you tilt or roll up.
A Tawa is a flat iron griddle for rotis; a Frying Pan has raised sides, for eggs.
A Fan just moves air from the ceiling; a Cooler is a box with water and grass pads that blows cool air.
A Matchbox has sticks you strike; a Lighter has a flint and gas and you flick it.
A Kettle heats water; a Flask keeps chai hot for hours.
A Glass is for water and has no handle; a Cup is for chai and has a handle.
A Bucket holds the water in the bathroom; a Mug is what you pour it over yourself with.
A Mixer Grinder has jars and blades for chutneys and masalas; a Toaster browns bread slices that pop up.
A Pressure Cooker is sealed and whistles; a Kadai is an open, deep wok.
A Fridge keeps food cold; a Microwave heats it up.
A Blanket goes on top of you to keep you warm; a Bedsheet covers the mattress.
A Sofa has a frame and seats several people; a Bean Bag is a squishy sack for one.
A Rolling Pin rolls out rotis; a Chopping Board is where you cut vegetables.
A Tap fills the bucket at waist height; a Shower sprays from overhead.
A Doormat is small, at the entrance, for wiping your feet; a Carpet covers the living-room floor.
An Almirah is a steel cupboard for clothes and valuables; a Shoe Rack sits by the door for footwear.
A Dustbin holds rubbish; a Laundry Basket holds dirty clothes.
A Hanger holds clothes in the cupboard; a Clothes Peg clips them on the drying line.
A Geyser heats bath water; an Inverter gives backup power during cuts.
A Plate is flat, for roti and sabzi; a Bowl is deep, for dal.
A Spoon scoops; a Fork has prongs that stab.
A Toothbrush cleans teeth; a Comb tidies hair.
An AC cools the room in summer; a Room Heater warms it in winter.
A Lock keeps the door shut and needs a key; a Doorbell rings when someone visits.
Both are glass. A Mirror shows you yourself; a Window shows you outside.
Both come out in a power cut. A Candle has a flame and wax; a Torch has a battery and a bulb.
A Clock tells the time; a Calendar tells the date.
A Vacuum Cleaner sucks up dust from floors; a Washing Machine cleans clothes.
